sections.title: Look Up (New Teaching)
paragraphs: Read
Throughout the world there are many people who suffer physically. Even in our suffering, we should choose to praise God.
Philippians 1:29
Job 1:1-22, Job 2:1-10 ( Job’s Suffering)
Tell It as a Story
Can someone tell this story in their own words?
Practice in groups of two.
Teach
Job was a godly man who turned away from sin.
Job was blessed with a family and many possessions.
Job cared greatly for his family.
Satan cannot do anything without God’s permission.
God is in control in all things.
God allowed Job to be tested by Satan.
Satan took Job’s property and the life of his children.
Through suffering, Job did not sin, and he continued to worship God.
Satan attacked Job’s health and gave him a skin disease.
Job’s wife told him to curse God, but he chose to trust God through the suffering he received.
Ask
What did you learn from these Scriptures?
Think a little, how will you practice what you have learned?

sections.title: Look Forward (Obedience)
paragraphs: Make a Plan
Commit to worship and praise Jesus even as you suffer.
Memorize James 1:2-3, which says, “Count it all joy, my brothers, when you meet trials of various kinds, for you know that the testing of your faith produces steadfastness.”
To whom will you tell your testimony and Jesus’ story?
Vision Casting
God desires that His gospel would be known among all people as a testimony. Let’s commit to share it with the world.
Matthew 24:14
Pray
Pray and ask God to help each of us face persecution with courage.
